speaker: Dr. Rajeeb Hazra, CEO of Quantinuum

checkins.note: Interim milestone Helios (≈100 physical qubits, two-qubit gate error <5×10⁻⁴) launched commercially per Quantinuum's Nov 2025 announcements, one step on the path to Apollo -- named here as the check-in to track, not as evidence the 2030 claim itself has resolved.
checkins.author: desk

verbatim: Quantinuum's roadmap unveils its fifth-generation quantum computer, Apollo, which will be a fully fault-tolerant and universal quantum computer, capable of executing circuits with millions of gates, delivering scientific advantage and enabling a commercial tipping point.
headline: Quantinuum will deliver universal, fully fault-tolerant quantum computing (system “Apollo”) by 2030.
resolution_criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if Quantinuum has, by 31 Dec 2030, shipped or publicly operated a system matching the Apollo specification (universal, fully fault-tolerant, circuits of millions of gates) -- confirmed by a Quantinuum announcement plus independent technical reporting. Note the press release's own text separately targets Apollo itself for 2029, one year ahead of the “by 2030” headline claim; both dates are logged so either can be checked against what actually ships. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if an earlier-generation system (Helios, Sol) ships on schedule but Apollo itself is delayed past 2030. NOT_VERIFIED otherwise.
